# Canonical MSE Thesis Writing Guardrails

Use this only for the Power–Electrified Transportation extreme-heat thesis. The live GitHub thesis authority index controls if a formal amendment has been approved. Do not change any frozen wording to make a paragraph sound more polished.

## Frozen title
Physics-Based Mathematical Engineering of Power–Transportation Interdependencies for Resilience

## Frozen general objective — verbatim
To characterize and model thermal interdependencies between the Power System and the Electrified Transportation System under extreme heat, and to quantify how their consequences evolve through physical state and time.

## Specific objectives — verbatim
SO1: Identify and qualify the thermally sensitive physical states and directional thermal interdependency mechanisms connecting the Power System and the Electrified Transportation System.

SO2: Develop a physics-based state-time model of the qualified thermal interdependencies and their propagation under extreme heat.

SO3: Quantify critical transition times, interdependency propagation delays, and the resulting electricity and mobility service consequences.

## Frozen research scope
Only thermal interdependencies between distinct Power and Electrified Transportation Systems under extreme heat, through state and time. Grid-connected battery-electric road charging is a bounded working case, not a redefinition of the entire transportation system. Electrical transfer and charging demand are admitted only to represent a qualified thermal mechanism or its consequence. Each direction requires independent qualification.

## Frozen resilience definition
Resilience is the ability of the coupled Power and Electrified Transportation systems to maintain or recover required electricity and mobility services as thermal states and thermal interdependencies evolve over time.

Improve, Adapt, Restore are engineering response classes supporting resilience; not new primary objectives. Evaluate response **effectiveness** through service maintenance or recovery if supported.

## Frozen sustainability definition
Sustainability in this thesis is assessed through two pathways: (1) the direct environmental, economic, and social consequences of thermal interdependencies on electricity and mobility services, and (2) the environmental, economic, and social consequences of engineering responses used to improve, adapt, or restore those services. Both pathways are evaluated within a declared system boundary and time horizon.

Energy efficiency belongs to environmental sustainability; resilience improvement does not guarantee sustainability improvement. No automatic single sustainability score. Avoid a full LCA or general optimization expansion.

## Model and evidence controls
- Heat forcing is not an internal state. SOC is an energy state, not a temperature. State ≠ capability ≠ service ≠ resilience ≠ sustainability.
- A physical connection or common exposure is not proof of directional thermal interdependency.
- Exact active states, parameters, thresholds, metrics, equipment, interventions, research questions, hypotheses, model and novelty claims remain OPEN until qualified and approved.
- Do not change the frozen General Objective or SO1–SO3 even by one word. Proposed new equations must be labeled candidate.
